chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
Nor is there a postponement (of payment) for his debt.
Nor is there a division of his belongings.
Nor is there discharge (of obligations) on his behalf.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a deceased person's debts and obligations in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that posthumous estate distribution is strictly limited to the settlement of blood money (diyah) or blood debt, excluding general manumission or debt postponement. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific financial obligations tied to the deceased's soul or estate take precedence over discretionary bequests, ensuring that divine rights (Huquq Allah) and human rights (Huquq al-Nas) are prioritized before any voluntary acts of charity or debt relief.
